references.text: Isaiah prophesies about the Lord as a shepherd who carries the lambs in his arms: 'Like a shepherd he will tend his flock. In his arm he gathers the lambs; he carries them close to his heart' (Isaiah 40:11). This is a prophetic background for the image of the shepherd placing the found sheep on his shoulders.

Ezekiel describes God as one who will himself seek out his sheep, care for them, rescue them, and look after them: 'I myself will search for my sheep and look after them... I will rescue them' (Ezekiel 34:11-16). Luke 15:5 shows Jesus as the fulfillment of this prophecy about the good shepherd.

Psalm 23 describes the Lord as a shepherd who leads, restores, and cares for his sheep (Psalm 23:1-3). The image of the shepherd finding and carrying the sheep on his shoulders in Luke 15:5 reflects that same caring shepherd-sheep relationship.

Jesus calls himself the good shepherd who gives his life for the sheep and knows each one by name (John 10:11-14). This expands on the image in Luke 15:5 of the shepherd personally seeking out and carrying the lost sheep.

Peter writes: 'You were like stray sheep, but now you have turned back to the Shepherd and Guardian of your souls' (1 Peter 2:25). The theme of stray sheep being found and brought back connects directly to the parable of the lost sheep.

'We all went astray like sheep; each one followed his own way' (Isaiah 53:6). This text describes humanity's condition as lost sheep – precisely the situation the shepherd in Luke 15:5 addresses by finding and carrying the sheep home.
The immediate context where Jesus asks who would not go after the one lost sheep (Luke 15:3-4) forms the basis for verse 5, where the joy of finding the sheep is described.

After placing the sheep on his shoulders, the shepherd gathers his friends and shares his joy – and Jesus uses this as an image of the joy in heaven over one sinner who repents (Luke 15:6-7). The joy in verse 5 points directly forward to the heavenly joy in verse 7.

God promises to set one shepherd over his sheep, his servant David (Ezekiel 34:23-24). Jesus fulfills this prophecy as the one shepherd who personally seeks out and carries his sheep, as illustrated in Luke 15:5.
